fact_claims.verbatim: Halcyon’s figures are 8.1 thermal incidents per 100,000 installed units company-wide last year
Our flagship’s 55 °C test failure rate is 3.9%.

S1_incident_reporting.quote: Manufacturers must report to the relevant regulator any thermal runaway, fire, explosion, injury, evacuation, or material property damage involving a unit within 24 hours of learning of it, followed by a preliminary investigation report within 10 business days and a final report within 30 days or when the investigation concludes. Suspected thermal incidents without injury or damage must be reported within 10 business days. Manufacturers must notify affected customers promptly, and no later than 5 business days after determining that a safety notice or action is warranted.

S2_thermal_testing.quote: A model with a failure rate above 5% must promptly notify the regulator and submit a corrective-action plan with milestones. Exceeding 5% alone does not automatically prohibit sale or require withdrawal of existing units; restrictions must be based on an individualized safety assessment and proportionate corrective action.

S3_remote_shutoff.quote: All newly installed systems must include a remotely operable emergency shut-off, with safeguards against unauthorized activation and a locally accessible shut-off as backup. Existing installed units must be brought into compliance or replaced within 6 years of this standard taking effect; where retrofit is technically infeasible, the manufacturer must provide an equivalent safety measure approved by the regulator.

S4_fire_suppression.quote: New home battery systems must include built-in fire suppression no later than 36 months after this standard takes effect. The suppression system must be suitable for the battery chemistry and installation, and must be tested under a regulator-approved protocol.

S5_customer_disclosure.quote: A manufacturer must initiate a mandatory recall when any model exceeds 8 thermal incidents per 100,000 installed units in any rolling 12-month period. The manufacturer must notify the regulator and affected customers promptly, explain the risk and remedy, and provide the remedy at no cost.

document.section_notes: S2 sets a 5% failure-rate benchmark but expressly does not stop sales or require withdrawal of existing units, which largely protects Northwind's Hearth 10 (6.2%). S5 keeps the 8-per-100,000 mandatory recall trigger with no transition, which directly binds Halcyon's Ember 8 (9.9), though notices are only 'promptly'. S3's 6-year retrofit and S4's 36-month suppression deadline sit inside the acceptable ranges, not the safe ones.
